title: Printing a Grid
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to print a 2D list so it looks like a neat grid on the screen.
learn: Join cells with spaces for a clean look
Nested loops help format the board
idea: Printing grid all at once shows Python's list brackets. For a game board look, print one row per line. You can print each row list, or loop through cells and print them with spaces so the grid lines up.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the separator " " to "-" in the line builder. Press Run. The bottom grid should look like 1-2-3- on each row.

practice.text: Print each row of the grid on its own line.
practice.hint: Loop over grid once. Each time through, print one row so you get three lines of output.
practice.starterTip: Add for row in grid: and on the next line (indented) print(row).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a for loop prints each row on a separate line.

practice.text: Print the board so each row shows three cells separated by spaces (use print with commas or build a line).
practice.hint: You need three printed lines — one per row. Commas in print() put spaces between values on the same line.
practice.starterTip: Try for row in board: then print(row[0], row[1], row[2]) so each row looks like X O X.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if each of the three rows is printed in a readable spaced format.

quiz.question: Why print one row per line?

options.text: So the grid looks like a table on screen
Because Python forbids printing whole lists
Rows cannot be printed any other way

quiz.correct: Row-by-row printing makes the board easy to read.
quiz.wrong: A vertical stack of rows looks like a real grid.

quiz.question: What does print(row[0], row[1], row[2]) do for a 3-cell row?

options.text: Prints the three cells with spaces

quiz.correct: print with commas separates values with spaces.
quiz.wrong: Comma-separated print values appear on one line with spaces.

quiz.question: On a 3x3 board, how many lines of row output should you usually see?
quiz.correct: Three rows mean three printed lines.
quiz.wrong: One print per row gives three lines.

project.title: Pretty Tic-Tac-Toe
project.desc: Make a 3x3 board with some X and O marks. Print it neatly — one row per line with spaces between cells.
